title: Thumbelina, the tiny little girl.
lines: Once upon a time there was a woman who really wanted a child.
One day an old fairy gave her a seed.
Plant this seed in a flower pot, said the fairy.
The woman planted the seed and watered it.
Soon a beautiful tulip grew, red and yellow.
The woman kissed the flower, and pop!
The tulip opened.
And in the middle of the flower sat a tiny little girl.
She was no bigger than a thumb.
That's why the woman called her Thumbelina.
Thumbelina slept in half a walnut shell, with a rose petal for a blanket.
During the day she sat in a tulip petal on a plate of water and rowed back and forth, and she sang so beautifully.
But one night a big, wet toad jumped in through the window.
Croak!
That girl is pretty, croaked the toad.
She must marry my son!
And she took the walnut shell with Thumbelina to the stream.
She put Thumbelina on a big water lily leaf, in the middle of the water.
Thumbelina cried.
She didn't want to live with the toads.
But the little fish in the stream had heard her.
They nibbled through the stem of the leaf.
And the leaf floated away, far away, with Thumbelina on it.
A beautiful white butterfly fluttered along with her.
All summer long Thumbelina lived alone in the forest.
She drank dewdrops and ate sweet honey from the flowers.
But then autumn came, and winter.
It got cold.
Brrr!
It snowed.
Thumbelina was so cold.
She knocked at the house of a field mouse.
May I come in?
she asked.
Of course, said the field mouse.
Come in, it's warm at my place.
One day Thumbelina found a swallow in the tunnel under the ground.
The swallow lay very still.
He was almost frozen.
Thumbelina laid a warm blanket of hay over him, and every day she gave him water.
And look, the swallow got better!
When spring came, the swallow said: Thank you, dear Thumbelina.
Come, come with me.
Thumbelina climbed onto his back, and they flew away together, high through the sky, over forests and mountains, to a warm land full of flowers.
In every flower lived a tiny little person, just as small as her!
And the flower prince gave her a pair of sparkling little wings.
Now Thumbelina could fly herself.
And the swallow came to visit her every year and sang her a song.
